title: Detect BCM43xx, T2, Vulkan, and NVIDIA via sysfs helpers
head: c2df703cf2a5
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The clean merge with open #11311 silently disables BCM4322 firmware installation on fresh installs
leads.consequence: #11311's added BCM4322 branch still tests $pci_info, but this PR removed its only assignment. The 3-way merge is conflict-free and contains both branches, yet a synthetic 14e4:432b device results in exit 0 and no b43-firmware package command. Fresh installs also mark migrations complete at provisioning, so #11311's separate upgrade migration will not repair the missed firmware. Preserve a sysfs-based BCM4322 branch while integrating #11311, and add a merged fixture.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus (Q5); published as finding

leads.summary: Security PR #9461 removes arch-mact2, but retaining this PR's pacman gate in the conflict restores an unsigned repo
leads.consequence: Open #9461 removes the unsigned arch-mact2 stanza and makes T2 package installation depend on signature-policy and package-origin preflight. The PRs are not stacked; the 3-way merge conflicts in both pacman.sh and fix-t2.sh. Resolving by keeping this PR's SigLevel = Never stanza and old omarchy-pkg-add transaction undoes #9461's security goal, while its fail-closed PCI enumeration is also lost if only this PR's predicate is kept. post-install/pacman.sh sources the stanza after overwriting pacman.conf. This PR does not newly introduce the unsigned policy in isolation. If #9461 lands, retain its signed-source policy, preflight, and pinned transaction, and reconcile the detector without turning PCI errors into silent non-T2 results.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified sol/pr-9461.diff removes arch-mact2 stanza and gh shows #9461 is draft; published as one related-PR bullet

leads.summary: Additional Broadcom Wi-Fi fixes in open PRs have no target in the new two-ID helper
leads.consequence: #11655 adds 14e4:43b1 (BCM4352), #10910 adds 14e4:4353 (BCM43224), and #10936 adds 14e4:4328/4329/432a (BCM4321) to the old install predicate. None is in the new helper. Their overlapping script merges conflict, so if any lands, resolving the hunk by retaining only this PR's helper call drops its added devices and broadcom-wl-dkms is not installed for them. Bring each accepted ID into the helper and adapt those PRs' lspci- or source-pattern-based tests. #12090's separate kernel-header change merges cleanly and is not part of this problem.
leads.triage: corroborated for #10910/#11655 (Opus); #10936 IDs verified by coordinator in sol/pr-10936.diff:82-98; published

leads.summary: The T2-only repo gate conflicts with #10306's firmware support on T2-less Macs
leads.consequence: #10306 expands the arch-mact2 gate to Apple machines with brcmfmac PCI IDs even without a T2, so the apple-bcm-firmware package it installs stays in a configured repository after the final pacman.conf restore. These PRs conflict at the condition. Resolving in favor of only omarchy-hw-t2 drops the non-T2 case, leaving the new firmware without its repository for subsequent updates. If #10306 is accepted, retain both conditions or reconcile with #9461's signed-repo replacement, rather than keeping only this PR's predicate.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified sol/pr-10306.diff pacman.sh gate widening; published as related-PR bullet

leads.summary: The unconditional AMD Vulkan branch conflicts with #10936's driver-bound eligibility guard
leads.consequence: Open #10936 adds an amdgpu-driver guard for AMD display cards and a test that expects no vulkan-radeon on radeon-bound or unbound cards. The same file produces a two-sided merge conflict. If its guard is dropped in favor of this PR's unconditional vendor match, those added tests fail. At Mesa 26.2.2 RADV explicitly rejects DRM devices not using the amdgpu driver; an installed vulkan-radeon ICD alone still makes omarchy-hw-vulkan report success. Adapt the guard within the sysfs scan if both are merged.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified sol/pr-10936.diff amd_gpu_on_amdgpu guard; published as related-PR bullet (Mesa detail omitted)

leads.summary: Apple Silicon support PR #9835 adds a non-PCI Vulkan fallback absent from this sysfs-only loop
leads.consequence: #9835 adds `omarchy-hw-apple-silicon` and calls it to request vulkan-asahi independently of PCI enumeration. This PR instead requests vulkan-asahi only if a 0x106b PCI display device appears. The PRs are not stacked, and their Vulkan script merge conflicts. If the conflict is resolved using just this PR's loop, the fallback explicitly introduced by #9835 disappears, and its Apple Silicon install path no longer requests vulkan-asahi. Preserve the hardware-level fallback if #9835 lands.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus (Q1/Q5); wording corrected per self-check D8

leads.summary: The new NVIDIA test passes when the real installer guard is disabled
leads.consequence: This file only greps the source for helper names and absence of a particular lspci spelling. Replacing the outer `if omarchy-hw-nvidia; then` with `if false; then` leaves all assertions green, while no NVIDIA driver packages or modprobe/mkinitcpio settings are written on a supported machine. Exercise the installer under a synthetic NVIDIA device with omarchy-pkg-add and /etc writes stubbed into private paths, and assert positive and negative package choices.

leads.summary: The T2 test never proves vendor matching or the two install-time call sites execute
leads.consequence: Its positive fixtures all use Apple 106b and negative fixture changes only the device ID. Deleting the helper's Apple vendor comparison leaves all tests green, allowing a device with a coincidental 1801/1802 ID from another vendor to trigger T2 packages and the hardware repository. The call-site checks are textual, so they also would not detect a dead installer branch. Add a non-Apple 1801/1802 case and stubbed install-time package/repository assertions.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus mutants); published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: The BCM helper test passes if vendor validation is removed
leads.consequence: All nonempty fixtures use Broadcom 14e4; removing the vendor comparison leaves the tests green, so a foreign device with 43a0 or 4331 would install broadcom-wl-dkms. Add a fixture with the matching device ID under a different vendor and assert no detection.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus mutants); published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: The Vulkan test has no Apple-vendor case, and its Apple branch can be deleted without failure
leads.consequence: Intel, AMD+NVIDIA, and Intel audio are covered, but the changed 0x106b -> vulkan-asahi branch is not. Replacing that branch with a no-op leaves all assertions green. Add a synthetic 0x106b/0x03 PCI fixture to prove this branch while keeping the separate non-PCI Apple Silicon case conditional on #9835.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus mutant table, 0x106b arm); published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: The new T2 helper's SIGPIPE explanation refers to a -q option the replaced installer did not use
leads.consequence: The T2 install and pacman leaves formerly ran `lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null`, without -q. That grep consumes the full stream, rather than closing after an early match. The description may be true of a separate migration using grep -q, but it does not explain a failure in either replaced T2 installer check. Update the helper comment without weakening the independently verified config-space motivation.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus Q6); published in Rationale wording

limits: No actual Intel/Apple/NVIDIA hardware was probed; all executions used review.py with synthetic sysfs and private stub logs. The #9835/#10936 findings concern consequences of merging the open PRs. RADV rejection of radeon-bound devices was traced in upstream Mesa 26.2.2 source. The PCI subsystem was traced at Linux v7.0 and pciutils 3.15.0 (Arch packaging upstream/arch-pciutils/PKGBUILD:3).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** `omarchy-hw-bcm43xx` and `omarchy-hw-t2` detect the same BCM4360/BCM4331 and T2 hardware as the `lspci` checks they replace, and follow the existing `omarchy-hw-nvidia*` helpers (same `OMARCHY_PCI_DEVICES_PATH` override, `nullglob`, exit codes and sysfs value format). The PR applies cleanly to the current `quattro` tip. All four new tests pass on the head and on a synthetic merge with the tip, and fail on the merge base. On synthetic machine layouts, the old and new install scripts install the same packages and write the same files, except for the Vulkan differences below.

The main issue is that the NVIDIA test cannot detect a broken install gate. One open PR also merges cleanly but stops working after this change.

### `nvidia-hw-detect-test.sh` passes with a broken NVIDIA gate

The test only greps `nvidia.sh`, and never runs it. Its first check, `grep -Fq 'omarchy-hw-nvidia'`, already matches `omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp` at the merge base, and at the head it also matches the new comment on line 1. The second check, `! grep -Eq "lspci.*nvidia"`, is case-sensitive. Copies of the head that change only the gate line all pass the test:

| Gate line in `install/hardware/nvidia.sh` | Effect | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `if omarchy-hw-nvidia; then` (PR) | intended | passes |
| `if true; then` | enters the block on every machine | passes |
| `if omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp; then` | skips 580xx installs (Maxwell, Pascal, Volta) | passes |
| `if lspci \| grep -qi 'NVIDIA'; then` | back to `lspci` | passes |

**Impact:** a regression in the only line this test is named for would go unnoticed.

**Suggested change:** run `nvidia.sh` against synthetic sysfs devices with `omarchy-pkg-add` stubbed, as `vulkan-sysfs-test.sh` does, and assert the package choice. Its hardcoded `/etc` writes would also need an override or a rewritten copy. At minimum, match the whole gate line (for example `grep -qx 'if omarchy-hw-nvidia; then'`).

### Open PR #11311 merges cleanly but its BCM4322 check stops firing

#11311 adds a BCM4322 branch to `install/hardware/fix-bcm43xx.sh` that tests `echo "$pci_info" | grep -q "14e4:432b"`. This PR deletes the `pci_info=$(lspci -nn)` assignment. A three-way merge of both has no conflict markers, and install leaves run without `nounset`, so the branch silently never matches:

```text
#11311 alone:        pci_info=$(lspci -nn) -> 14e4:432b found -> b43-firmware requested from the AUR (when reachable)
#11311 + this PR:    pci_info unset        -> no match         -> nothing installed, exit 0
```

A sandboxed run of the merged script with a synthetic `14e4:432b` device exited 0 and requested no firmware package. `hw-bcm43xx-test.sh` would not catch this, because the merged file contains no `lspci` text.

**Impact:** if both land, fresh installs on BCM4322 machines never request `b43-firmware`, and nothing reports an error.

**Suggested change:** if both PRs are accepted, move the BCM4322 check to a sysfs read (for example a helper like `omarchy-hw-bcm43xx`) as part of combining them.

### Vulkan selection changes that the PR does not describe

| Machine | Old `(VGA\|Display).*<vendor>` regex | New PCI class `0x03*` + vendor ID |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic T2 Mac (Intel iGPU + AMD dGPU) | `vulkan-intel vulkan-asahi vulkan-radeon` | `vulkan-intel vulkan-radeon` |
| Intel or AMD GPU with class 0x0301 (XGA) or 0x0302 (3D controller) | nothing | vendor package installed |

On T2 Macs, `lspci -nn` shows `Non-VGA unclassified device [0000]: Apple Inc. T2 Bridge Controller [106b:1801]` (as quoted in #6608 and #6559). The old regex matched `VGA` inside `Non-VGA`, so every T2 Mac got `vulkan-asahi`, an Apple Silicon driver that is of no use there. Both changes look like improvements, but only a synthetic Intel 0x0302 case was run, and it was not matched to a real Intel or AMD GPU.

**Impact:** Vulkan package selection changes without being described in the PR. `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` (lines 786-787) and `migrations/1784401744.sh` (lines 24-25) keep the old regex, so fresh installs and upgraded T2 Macs will now select different packages.

**Suggested change:** state both changes in the PR description, and decide whether the upgrade paths should use the same detection.

**Unneeded heredoc rename:** changing the `nvidia.sh` heredoc delimiters from `EOF` to `NVEOF` writes byte-identical files. It is not in the predecessor PR #10806, and it is the only reason this PR conflicts with open PR #8263 (a copy of the head without the rename merges with #8263 cleanly). Dropping it avoids that conflict.

**Rationale wording:** the config-space reason is correct: `lspci` reads each device's config space, which can resume a runtime-suspended GPU, while the sysfs `vendor`, `device` and `class` files are cached. The SIGPIPE reason in the PR body and the `omarchy-hw-t2` comment does not apply to the replaced call sites. The old T2 checks used `grep ... >/dev/null` without `-q`, and install leaves run with `errexit` but without `pipefail`. Consider limiting the comment to the config-space reason. T2 detection also still uses `lspci` in `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh` (line 23), in the same install pass.

**Optional test improvement:** removing the vendor check from `omarchy-hw-bcm43xx` or `omarchy-hw-t2` leaves their tests green, and so does deleting the `0x106b` branch in `vulkan.sh`. A fixture with the right device ID under another vendor, and a `0x106b` display-class fixture, would cover those lines.

**Related open PRs:** these overlap the same detection and would need adapting after this change:
- **#9238** adds its own `bin/omarchy-hw-t2` using `lspci -nn | grep -q` (add/add conflict). It could reuse this helper.
- **#11259** is a competing sysfs design (shared `install/helpers/pci-sysfs.sh`). The draft **#12681** carries a copy of this PR plus a hot-unplug change.
- **#10910, #11655 and #10936** add Broadcom IDs to the old `fix-bcm43xx.sh` check. Accepted IDs would belong in `omarchy-hw-bcm43xx`.
- **#10306** widens the `arch-mact2` gate in `pacman.sh` to non-T2 Macs with brcmfmac Wi-Fi, and the draft **#9461** removes the unsigned `arch-mact2` repository. Keeping only this PR's side of those conflicts would drop their changes.
- **#10936** adds an `amdgpu`-driver guard to `vulkan.sh`, and **#9835** replaces the Apple PCI match there with Apple Silicon device-tree detection. Both conflict with the new sysfs loop.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head against the merge base and current `quattro` tip. The new and neighbouring hardware tests ran in an isolated sandbox against synthetic sysfs trees, and the full shell suites ran in the same sandbox with `/sys` hidden. The PR adds no failing test files; the suites have the same pre-existing failures before and after the change. Old and new install scripts were compared on synthetic machine layouts with a stubbed `lspci`, stubbed package installs and redirected `/etc` writes. The T2 `lspci` lines were modelled on public user reports; the other `lspci` lines are hand-written approximations. Merges with the tip and with open PRs touching these files were simulated. No physical hardware was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
